title: Hands-on_Ex02
text:
Importing Data

exam_data <- read_csv("/Users/zhanyi/Desktop/M Y1S2/ISSS608/ISSS608-VAA/project 1/ISSS608/Hands-on_Ex/Hands-on_Ex02/data/Exam_data.csv")


exam_data$MATHS <- as.numeric(exam_data$MATHS)


exam_data$ENGLISH <- as.numeric(exam_data$ENGLISH)

title: Hands-on_Ex02
text:
ggrepel

colnames(exam_data)

[1] "S/N"     "CLASS"   "NAME"    "GENDER"  "RACE"    "ENGLISH" "MATHS"  
[8] "SCIENCE"



# fixed the codes by replacing ID with NAME in the label
ggplot(data=exam_data, 
       aes(x= MATHS, 
           y=ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method=lm, 
              size=0.5) +  
  geom_label(aes(label = NAME), 
             hjust = .5, 
             vjust = -.5) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,100),
                  ylim=c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("English scores versus Maths scores for Primary 3")









ggplot(data=exam_data, 
       aes(x= MATHS, 
           y=ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method=lm, 
              size=0.5) +  
  geom_label_repel(aes(label = NAME), 
                   fontface = "bold") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,100),
                  ylim=c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("English scores versus Maths scores for Primary 3")

title: Hands-on_Ex02
text:
GGplot2

ggplot(data=exam_data, 
             aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=20, 
                 boundary = 100,
                 color="grey25", 
                 fill="grey90") +
  theme_gray() +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Maths scores")

title: Hands-on_Ex02
text:
GGtheme

ggplot(data=exam_data, 
             aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=20, 
                 boundary = 100,
                 color="grey25", 
                 fill="grey90") +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Maths scores") +
  theme_economist()

title: Hands-on_Ex02
text:
Hrbthems package

ggplot(data=exam_data, 
             aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=20, 
                 boundary = 100,
                 color="grey25", 
                 fill="grey90") +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Maths scores") +
  theme_ipsum()

title: Hands-on_Ex02
text:
Beyond Single Graphs

p1 <- ggplot(data=exam_data, 
             aes(x = MATHS)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=20, 
                 boundary = 100,
                 color="grey25", 
                 fill="grey90") + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Maths scores")


p2 <- ggplot(data=exam_data, 
             aes(x = ENGLISH)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=20, 
                 boundary = 100,
                 color="grey25", 
                 fill="grey90") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("Distribution of English scores")


p3 <- ggplot(data=exam_data, 
             aes(x= MATHS, 
                 y=ENGLISH)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method=lm, 
              size=0.5) +  
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,100),
                  ylim=c(0,100)) +
  ggtitle("English scores versus Maths scores for Primary 3")


Combining two ggplot2 graphs

p1 + p2










Combinig three ggplot2 graphs

(p1 / p2) | p3










Creating figure with insert

p3 + inset_element(p2, 
                   left = 0.02, 
                   bottom = 0.7, 
                   right = 0.5, 
                   top = 1)










Creating a composite figure by using patchwork and ggtheme

patchwork <- (p1 / p2) | p3
patchwork & theme_economist()
